The Road to Glory

Everyone Made the Playoffs. Some Deserved To.

Seven weeks of flag football have brought us extraordinary performances, questionable coaching decisions, suspicious statistical achievements, and an alarming number of injured Knudsons.

William Timpson finishes atop the standings at 6–1. Cole White enters with the league’s best point differential at +94. Donald Timpson somehow secured the third seed despite being outscored by 16 points over the regular season.

And Dylan Horsley, having successfully avoided victory for seven consecutive weeks, has been rewarded with a playoff berth.

In Loving Memory

Nathan & Derrick Knudson

Gone from the field, but never from our hearts.

It is with profound sadness that we announce Nathan Knudson has joined his beloved brother Derrick among those who are no longer with us on the football field.

Nathan’s season came to a tragic end following a broken collarbone, leaving behind teammates, friends, and a league struggling to come to terms with his absence.

While their time on the field was cut far too short, the memories they created will remain with us forever.

Though we must now continue without them, we take comfort in knowing that the brothers have been reunited on the sidelines.

Their seasons may have ended, but our love for them will never die.

Forever in our hearts. Forever Knudsons.

The Weather Report • Special Investigation

Levi Knudson Faces Unfair Scrutiny as League Ignores the Elements

Following an uncharacteristically poor performance, Levi Knudson has found himself at the center of an increasingly unfair media narrative. Critics have questioned his accuracy, decision-making, and suspicious absence the following week. What they have conveniently ignored are the brutal weather conditions under which he was expected to perform.

Cold temperatures. Unpredictable winds. The possibility of precipitation.

Our editorial staff believes it is irresponsible to evaluate a quarterback without accounting for circumstances entirely outside his control. Unfortunately, Saturday’s Colorado City forecast calls for approximately 50°F and cloudy skies. The possibility of lingering atmospheric effects, however, cannot be ruled out.

Meanwhile, Gilbert Cawley faces problems of his own. With Nathan Knudson out for the season, Gilbert has lost one of his most dependable receivers. Is Gilbert actually an accurate quarterback, or has he simply benefited from receivers capable of catching anything thrown in their general direction?

Two quarterbacks. Two very different challenges. One missing his favorite receiver. The other potentially missing his confidence.

Our investigative department will check back after this week’s games to determine whether Levi showed up and whether Gilbert managed to complete a pass without Nathan Knudson.

EXHIBIT A • Forecast screenshot supplied for the playoff preview
The Left-Handed Miracle

Jay Timpson’s Hands May Finally Work Again

For three consecutive seasons, Jay Timpson enjoyed the luxury of playing with left-handed quarterbacks. This year, forced to adjust to the unnatural spin of a right-handed football, Jay’s receiving production became a matter of league-wide concern.

Fortunately, the playoffs offer new hope. Jay’s team faces Gilbert Cawley, a left-handed quarterback whose throwing motion should feel comfortingly familiar. Unfortunately, Gilbert plays for the opposing team.

League officials have not confirmed whether Jay intends to switch teams, intercept a pass, or simply stand close enough to Gilbert to feel the familiar left-handed energy.

The evidence is compelling. When left-handed Alonso “Lonnie” Timpson substituted for Joseph’s team as Sub Joseph, Jay recorded seven receptions, 149 yards, and two touchdowns.

Apparently Jay’s hands work perfectly well. They simply have a preferred rotational direction.
The Investigative Unit

Donald vs. Cole vs. Lonnie: A Family Hierarchy Emerges

Donald Timpson held Cole White to just two receiving yards in Week 7. Cole then appeared as a substitute on Dylan’s side against Alonso “Lonnie” Timpson, where the result was considerably less flattering for Lonnie.

Donald stopped Cole. Lonnie could not stop Cole.

After an exhaustive investigation, our department has reached the only reasonable conclusion: Donald Timpson is the more athletic brother, and Father Time may finally be catching up with Lonnie.

Lonnie is reportedly seeking a second opinion and a younger pair of ankles.

The Commissioner’s Statistical Empire

Donald finishes the season with a league-leading 58 receptions and 87 targets, along with 870 yards and 12 receiving touchdowns. The fact that the commissioner’s brothers are involved in keeping statistics has done little to quiet speculation.

We are not alleging wrongdoing. We are simply observing that Donald gets the ball more than anyone else, puts up excellent numbers, and has family members keeping track of it all. The investigation remains open.

The Seeding Anomaly: Donald Timpson, Third Seed, Negative Point Differential, Absolutely No Questions Asked

In one of the more remarkable mathematical developments of the season, Commissioner Donald Timpson secured the No. 3 playoff seed despite finishing with a −16 point differential.

Curiously, Gilbert Cawley (+40) and Joseph M. Timpson (+25) finished with identical 4–3 records, yet somehow find themselves seeded fourth and fifth.

Our investigative department has been unable to identify a mathematical explanation for this arrangement. When asked for clarification, league officials reportedly referred investigators to the commissioner.

The commissioner is Donald Timpson.

The investigation has been closed due to a conflict of interest.

Brotherly Love

Willy vs. George: The Matchup That Never Was

Willy and George Timpson are both quick, competitive brothers. Fans wanted to see them line up against one another and settle the family debate.

Unfortunately, Willy apparently shared none of that enthusiasm. Despite the opportunity to settle years of sibling debate, he was reportedly far too frightened to cover George.

The league has classified the incident as a strategic avoidance maneuver. George’s speed remains unquestioned. Willy’s confidence remains under investigation.

Gilbert Cawley Longevity Watch

Still Active. Somehow.

In a development that continues to astonish medical professionals, historians, and anyone familiar with the invention of color television, Gilbert Cawley remains on an active roster entering the playoffs.

Through seven games: 1,736 passing yards and 26 touchdowns. At an age when most athletes have transitioned to coaching, golfing, or increasingly exaggerated stories about their playing days, Gilbert continues to throw touchdowns.

League historians are researching whether Gilbert was already playing organized football when Joseph was born. He is certainly old enough to remember Jay’s birth.

Week 7 • Final Scoreboard

Last Calls Before the Postseason

William’s Team / Gilbert’s Team44–34

William threw for 315 yards and five touchdowns; Gilbert countered with 331 yards and five scores. Only one came away with the win.

Joseph’s Team / Aaron’s Team54–40

Alonso “Lonnie” Timpson, listed as Sub Joseph, threw for 372 yards and seven touchdowns. Jay’s seven catches, 149 yards, and two scores were apparently unlocked by left-handed spin.

Donald’s Team / Cole’s Team34–25

Daniel Dockstader threw for 293 yards and five touchdowns. Cole caught two passes for two yards. The commissioner’s athletic superiority case rests comfortably on this exhibit.

Alonso’s Team / Dylan’s Team32–26

Alonso threw for 346 yards and five touchdowns; Dylan Horsley threw for 348 yards and four. Cole’s substitute appearance on Dylan’s team adds to the investigative intrigue, but the passing totals belong to Dylan.

The Offensive Recession

Dylan Horsley Declares Bankruptcy

Dylan’s team finishes 0–7 with a −171 point differential. Seven weeks, seven losses, and no signs of recovery. Donald’s team, meanwhile, has secured the third seed with a −16 differential. Dylan’s team is clearly in recession; Donald’s appears to be operating under an economic system nobody else understands.

Steal of the Draft

Aaron Zitting • Round 7

Six sacks. Nobody in the league finished with more, and Aaron was still waiting in Round 7.

Biggest Draft Bust

Caleb Barlow • Round 2

Standing 6'2" with a 37-inch vertical, Caleb Barlow entered the season with enormous expectations. In just four games, he recorded 18 receptions, 317 receiving yards, and five touchdowns — an average of roughly 79 receiving yards per appearance. Despite these numbers, the award committee unanimously named Caleb the Biggest Draft Bust of 2026. No further explanation was provided.

From the Editorial Desk

The regular season is over. The excuses have been documented. The investigations remain open.

And somewhere, Gilbert Cawley is preparing for yet another football game.
